story.title: Israeli Election Results Show No Clear Winner Amid Seat Losses for Netanyahu
story.summary: Israel's recent elections have resulted in no clear winner, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition losing a significant number of seats compared to the 2022 election. Despite high voter turnout, projections indicate that opposition parties have gained more seats, but they lack the majority needed to form a government, leading to potential coalition negotiations in the coming weeks.

timeline_highlights.title: Netanyahu's Bloc Leads Israeli Election, But Majority Remains Elusive
timeline_highlights.summary: As of the latest counts, Netanyahu's right-wing bloc is leading the Israeli election but is falling short of the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset. With over 85% of the votes counted, projections indicate that Netanyahu's Likud party and its allies are set to secure around 53 seats, while the opposing coalition led by Eisenkot is expected to gain approximately 48 seats, alongside 19 seats for Arab-led parties. The results suggest a potential deadlock, prompting calls from President Isaac Herzog to avoid another election.
key_facts: Netanyahu's bloc leads with approximately 53 seats projected.
No coalition is expected to reach the majority of 61 seats.
President Herzog urges against a new election.

explore_lenses.label: What do the results establish so far?
explore_lenses.title: Partial returns, not a final seat allocation
explore_lenses.summary: As of October 28, the available picture is still provisional: broadcasters' projections and partial vote counts indicate neither main bloc has a straightforward 61-seat route, while official results are not due until November 4.

claims.text: With about 85% of votes counted, AP reported local projections of 53 seats for Likud and its allies, 48 for Eisenkot's bloc, and 19 for Arab-led parties; these were projections rather than certified results.
The Central Elections Committee says final results for the 26th Knesset are to be published by November 4, 2026.
Uncounted absentee ballots, including ballots from military personnel and diplomats, mean the final distribution of seats could still differ from election-night projections.

points: With about 85% of votes counted, AP reported local projections of 53 seats for Likud and its allies, 48 for Eisenkot's bloc, and 19 for Arab-led parties; these were projections rather than certified results.
The Central Elections Committee says final results for the 26th Knesset are to be published by November 4, 2026.
Uncounted absentee ballots, including ballots from military personnel and diplomats, mean the final distribution of seats could still differ from election-night projections.

explore_lenses.label: Why are Arab-led parties central to talks?
explore_lenses.title: Their projected seats could decide the majority
explore_lenses.summary: Arab-led parties' unusually strong projected showing makes their support or tolerance potentially decisive, but political vetoes—not just arithmetic—complicate that route.

claims.text: AP reported that Arab-led parties had 14.9% of counted votes and were projected to hold 19 seats, enough to be pivotal when neither of the two larger blocs is near 61 alone.
Netanyahu said he would not partner with Arab-led parties and described a government including them as dangerous; AP reported those parties had also ruled out partnering with him.

Eisenkot left open cooperation with Arab-led parties under conditions including recognizing Israel as a Jewish state and Hamas as an extremist group, but AP reported that some of his prospective partners had ruled out such an alliance.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next procedurally?
explore_lenses.title: Certification, presidential consultations, coalition deadline
explore_lenses.summary: After results are published, President Isaac Herzog consults parliamentary groups and assigns an MK the task of forming a government; failure can trigger further mandates and, ultimately, another election.

claims.text: The Knesset states that within seven days of publication of election results, the president must assign an MK the task of forming a government.
The first designee has 28 days to form a government, and the president may extend that period by up to 14 additional days.
The president is not legally required to choose the leader of the largest party; the choice follows consultations with the parliamentary groups.

Forecast: AP reported that, if no candidate assembles a majority coalition, another election could be held in early 2027; Reuters reported that Netanyahu was expected to remain caretaker prime minister during negotiations.

story_report.summary: Israel’s election produced no decisive path to government, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition losing substantial ground from 2022 and opposition parties gaining seats without reaching a majority. With roughly 85% of votes counted, local projections put Likud and its allies at 53 seats, an Eisenkot-led bloc at 48, and Arab-led parties at 19. The fragmented result points to difficult coalition negotiations after final results are published.

sections.heading: Arab-Led Parties Hold Potential Leverage
sections.body: Arab-led parties were projected to win 19 seats, after receiving 14.9% of counted votes, making them potentially pivotal because neither larger bloc was close to the 61 seats needed to govern alone. Netanyahu said he would not partner with those parties and called a government including them dangerous; AP reported that the parties had also ruled out joining him. Eisenkot left open conditional cooperation, though some prospective Jewish-party partners had rejected such an alliance.

sections.heading: Government Formation Process Begins After Results
sections.body: Under the Knesset’s rules, the president must task a member of parliament with forming a government within seven days of publication of the election results, following consultations with parliamentary groups. The first designee has 28 days, with a possible extension of up to 14 days. The president is not legally required to select the leader of the largest party; Reuters reported Netanyahu was expected to remain caretaker prime minister during negotiations.

unresolved.text: Final party totals and the seat allocation were not certified as of October 28. Absentee ballots, including votes from military personnel and diplomats, could still alter the election-night projections; final results are scheduled for publication by November 4, 2026.

It remains uncertain whom President Herzog will first ask to form a government, whether that candidate can win Knesset confidence, and whether outside support or cooperation involving Arab-led parties can be arranged. If no candidate can assemble a majority coalition, AP reported another election could be held in early 2027.

She had been held on remand for seven years following charges related to an alleged attempt to murder her former husband, Constantino Chiwenga, in 2019.
